sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that, petitioner claims to be owner, possessor and enjoyer of the agriculture land of an extent of Ac.0-16 cents in SY.No.131/2C, Maddinayanapalli Panchayat, Pakala Mandal, Tirupati District.
The name of the petitioner was mutated in the revenue records and pattadar passbooks were also issued in his favour.
The petitioner has been in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject land without any interruption whatsoever.
The petitioner submits that,
Respondent Nos.2 to 4 are trying to NV,J interfere into the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the petitioner's subject land
. Questioning the inaction of Respondent Nos.2 to 4, the present writ petition is filed.

3. Learned Government Pleader for Revenue placed on record written instructions furnished by the Tahsildar, Pakala Mandal dated 02.05.2025, wherein it is submitted that land in Sy.No.131/2 with a total extent of Ac.0.33 cents is classified as Government Wet Patta as per A Register of maddinayanapalli Village.

As per webland adangal the land inSy.No.131/2A, extent Ac.0-16 cents stands in favour of B. Vasu vide Khata No.878 and the land in Sy.No.131/2B, with an extent of Ac.0-17 cents stands in favour of A. Keerthisekhar s/o Raghunandaiah vide Khata No.232 of Maddinayanapalli Village of Pakala Mandal, Tirupati District.

Further it is to submit that the petitioner has encroached the land in Sy.No.131/1 to an extent of Ac.0-04 cents by the way of constructing RCC rooms and is adjacent to the subject land which is classified as Tank Poramboke as per A Register with a total extent of Ac.5-94 cents.
Further, Respondent Nos.2 to 4 did not interfere into the possession and enjoyment over the subject land in Sy.No.131/2 in any manner.

4. During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioner, without touching the merits of the case,
requested this Court to issue a direction to the respondents not to dispossess the petitioner from his land without following due process of law.
NV,J 5.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submits that, the respondents would follow due process of law and requested to pass appropriate orders.
6. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Revenue and perused the material available on record.
